title: The Tale of the Stolen Necklace (简体中文)

keywords: the tale of the stolen necklace
full_text:
Queen Tirumala Devi, while bathing in the royal pleasure pavilion on the palace grounds, left her priceless necklace of five strands of Basra pearls upon an open silver tray by the veranda window.
When she emerged from her bath, the necklace had vanished!
The palace guards searched the rooms in panic. Suspicion immediately fell upon the three young maidservants who had attended the Queen.
The Chief Chamberlain was preparing to throw the weeping maidens into prison when Tenali Raman arrived.

Tenali inspected the open window.
He examined the stone sill: there were no human footprints, but on the polished ledge he found two small, distinctive scratch marks, and on the grass below lay a single bitten neem fruit.
Looking up, Tenali saw an ancient gulmohar tree whose branches overhung the window, where a troop of wild rhesus monkeys frequently played.

Tenali said: 'Chamberlain, release the maidservants. The thief is not human.'

Tenali knew that if guards climbed the tree with sticks, the frightened monkeys would scatter across the city roofs and the necklace would be lost forever in the river or bushes.

Tenali devised a clever, peaceful strategy.
He brought twenty strings of cheap, glittering glass bead necklaces from the market and a large basket of ripe yellow bananas.
He walked beneath the gulmohar tree and began tossing bananas and glass necklaces onto the grass, wearing one glass necklace around his own neck, dancing and making joyful sounds.

The curious monkeys descended to the lower branches.
One large male monkey was sitting on a high bough, proudly holding the Queen's pearl necklace around its neck!
Seeing the other monkeys picking up bananas and wearing the shiny glass beads, the monkey grew jealous.
Tenali took off his own glass necklace, made a dramatic flourish, and tossed it into the soft grass, walking away.

The monkey on the bough immediately mimicked Tenali's motion:
It took off the heavy pearl necklace, tossed it down into the grass to grab a shiny glass necklace and two bananas!

Tenali’s attendants immediately scooped up the pearl necklace undamaged!
The Queen wept with joy upon receiving her heirloom, the innocent maidens were rewarded with gold coins for their distress, and King Krishnadevaraya praised Tenali’s patient understanding of animal behavior.
moral: Patience and understanding the habits of nature recover lost treasures where brute force fails. [ZH]
